policyQuote: Molecular Data Usage: "...NCBI itself places no restrictions on the use or distribution of the data contained therein. Nor do we accept data when the submitter has requested restrictions on reuse or redistribution. However, some submitters of the original data (or the country of origin of such data) may claim patent, copyright, or other intellectual property rights in all or a portion of the data (that has been submitted). NCBI is not in a position to assess the validity of such claims ... Therefore, NCBI cannot provide comment or unrestricted permission concerning the use, copying, or distribution of the information contained in the molecular databases." Copyright Status of Webpages: "Information that is created by or for the US government on this site is within the public domain. Public domain information on the National Library of Medicine (NLM) Web pages may be freely distributed and copied. However, it is requested that in any subsequent use of this work, NLM be given appropriate acknowledgment."

citation: Kim S, Chen J, Cheng T, Gindulyte A, He J, He S, Li Q, Shoemaker BA, Thiessen PA, Yu B, Zaslavsky L, Zhang J, Bolton EE. PubChem 2025 update. Nucleic Acids Res. 2025 Jan 6;53(D1):D1516-25. doi:10.1093/nar/gkae1059. PMID: 39558165.
citationPubChem3D: Bolton EE, Chen J, Kim S, Han L, He S, Shi W, Simonyan V, Sun Y, Thiessen PA, Wang J, Yu B, Zhang J, Bryant SH. PubChem3D: A new resource for scientists. J Cheminform. 2011 Sep 20; 3(1):32. doi: 10.1186/1758-2946-3-32. PMID: 21933373.
pubchem3dMethodQuote: "PubChem generates (with OpenEye's OMEGA) a computed 3-D description of each compound in the PubChem Compound database that is not too large (<= 50 non-hydrogen atoms), is not too flexible (<= 15 rotatable bonds), consists of only organic elements (H, C, N, O, F, Si, P, S, Cl, Br, and I), has a single covalent unit (i.e., not a salt or a mixture), and contains only atom types recognized by the MMFF94s force field." and "Each computed 3-D conformer is not at an energy minimum and may not represent the lowest energetic form in vacuum, solvent, or a binding pocket."
twoDCoordinateNote: All 2D records: z = 0, heavy-atom bonds exactly 1.00 drawing unit, bonds to H 0.62 units (HCl: 1.00). These are arbitrary drawing units, not angstroms; every 2D file with hydrogens would be rejected by validator rule 3 (H bond 0.62 < 0.80), which is the intended behaviour.

fieldNotes.twoDHasHydrogens: true = every hydrogen is an explicit atom with its own x,y in the 2D record; null = the molecule has no hydrogens. No entry is false.
fieldNotes.minHeavyBondA: null = no 3D record (has3d false) or no bond between two non-hydrogen atoms (H2O, NH3, CH4, HCl, H3O+).
fieldNotes.minHBondA: null = no 3D record or no hydrogens.
fieldNotes.atomOrder: For all 29 entries with both records, the 2D and 3D files list atoms in the same order with identical bond tables and charges (checked by extra.mjs), so 2D and 3D positions can be merged by index.

entries.name: Water
entries.notes: 3D (MMFF94s) O-H 0.969 A, H-O-H 103.98 deg. Spec builds Basics from experimental values instead, so the PubChem 3D file is reference only.

entries.name: Carbon dioxide
entries.notes: No hydrogens. 3D record is linear along one axis so every z is 0.0 even though it is a genuine 3D record: 'all z = 0' cannot be used to detect a 2D file. C=O 1.197 A in the computed model.

entries.name: Ammonia
entries.notes: IUPAC name returned is 'azane'. 3D N-H 1.019 A, H-N-H 106.0 deg.

entries.name: Methane
entries.notes: 3D C-H 1.0922 A, tetrahedral 109.47 deg. No heavy-atom bond.

entries.name: Oxygen (O2)
entries.notes: Stored as O=O (double bond, closed-shell Lewis structure, no radical markers); matches the spec's MO callout need. 3D z all 0 (diatomic). O=O 1.232 A in the computed model.

entries.name: Nitrogen (N2)
entries.notes: N#N triple bond. 3D z all 0 (diatomic). 1.112 A in the computed model.

entries.name: Hydrogen chloride
entries.notes: PubChem title for CID 313 is 'Hydrochloric Acid' and the IUPAC name returned is 'chlorane'; the structure is the HCl molecule. 2D record draws the H-Cl bond at 1.00 units (not 0.62 as for other H bonds). 3D H-Cl 1.3058 A.

entries.name: Hydrogen peroxide
entries.notes: 3D O-O 1.4494 A, O-H 0.9723 A, O-O-H 95.8 deg, H-O-O-H dihedral 94.0 deg (non-planar, as expected).

entries.name: Boron trifluoride
entries.notes: NO 3D RECORD (HTTP 404, PUGREST.NotFound; ConformerCount3D = 0). Boron is outside PubChem3D's supported element list. 2D record exists; no hydrogens. Matches the spec's statement; coordinates must come from the experimental-geometry build script.

entries.name: Sulfur dioxide
entries.notes: 3D record exists (200) but is planar with all z = 0. Stored as O=S=O (two double bonds, no formal charges) - this is the hypervalent Lewis form; the spec requires stating which Lewis structure is used. Computed S=O is 1.5697 A and O-S-O 113.0 deg; this MMFF94s geometry should not be used (spec already builds VSEPR group from experimental values).

entries.name: Sulfur hexafluoride
entries.notes: NO 3D RECORD (HTTP 404; ConformerCount3D = 0). Elements S and F are supported, so the cause is presumably the MMFF94s atom-type rule (hexavalent S) - PubChem does not state the reason per record. 2D record: 6 F around S in a flat hexagon.

entries.name: Xenon tetrafluoride
entries.notes: NO 3D RECORD (HTTP 404; ConformerCount3D = 0). Xe is outside PubChem3D's supported element list. 2D record: square-planar-looking cross, no lone pairs shown.

entries.name: Phosphorus pentachloride
entries.notes: NO 3D RECORD (HTTP 404; ConformerCount3D = 0). Elements P and Cl are supported, so presumably the MMFF94s atom-type rule (pentavalent P with 5 Cl). 2D record: flat irregular 5-spoke drawing (one P-Cl is 0.9999 units), not usable as a trigonal-bipyramid depiction.

entries.name: Ethene
entries.notes: PubChem title 'Ethylene', IUPAC name 'ethene'. 3D C=C 1.3344 A; planar molecule but the 3D record is not axis-aligned (z not all 0).

entries.name: Ethyne
entries.notes: PubChem title 'Acetylene' and the IUPACName property also returns 'acetylene' (not 'ethyne'). 3D C#C 1.200 A, C-H 1.065 A, linear (179.99 deg).

entries.name: Ethanol
entries.notes: One conformer only (ConformerCount3D = 1). 3D C-O 1.4198 A, O-H 0.9725 A.

entries.name: Acetic acid
entries.notes: 3D: C=O 1.2221 A, O-H 0.9811 A; O=C-O-H dihedral 0.0 deg (syn carboxylic acid).

entries.name: Acetone
entries.notes: IUPAC name 'propan-2-one'. 3D C=O 1.2299 A.

entries.name: Methylamine
entries.notes: IUPAC name 'methanamine'. 3D N is pyramidal (angle sum 326.0 deg). C-N 1.4308 A.

entries.name: Ethyl acetate
entries.notes: 9 conformers in PubChem3D; record_type=3d returns the first (default) conformer only - 'one conformer of many' note in the spec is warranted. 3D C=O 1.2237 A.

entries.name: Acetamide
entries.notes: 3D amide N is exactly planar (angle sum 360.0 deg), consistent with the spec's sp2 / trigonal-planar expectation. C=O 1.2286 A, N-H 1.0147 A.

entries.name: Benzene
entries.notes: Bond block is Kekule (alternating orders 1 and 2), there is NO aromatic bond type 4; the aromatic flag must be authored. 3D C-C all 1.3947-1.3949 A (equal), C-H 1.086 A.

entries.name: beta-D-Glucopyranose
entries.notes: PubChem title 'Beta-D-Glucose'; IUPAC name (2R,3R,4S,5S,6R)-6-(hydroxymethyl)oxane-2,3,4,5-tetrol; 5 of 5 stereocentres defined, 0 undefined. 7 conformers; default returned. 3D ring is a chair (ring torsions alternate about +/-55 deg, printed by build-json.mjs). 2D record carries 5 wedge/hash bonds (bond-block stereo column 1 or 6) and the chiral flag; parse-sdf.mjs deliberately ignores the stereo column, so wedges must be read separately if the Lewis view should show them. Shortest bonds: C-O 1.4159 A, O-H 0.9716 A.

entries.name: Glycine (neutral)
entries.notes: CID 750 is the neutral (non-zwitterion) form NCC(=O)O, IUPAC '2-aminoacetic acid', no M  CHG line. N pyramidal. Shares the same standard InChI as the zwitterion CID 5257127 (InChI normalises the mobile proton), so the two forms can only be told apart by CID / SMILES / charges, not by InChI or InChIKey.

entries.name: Glycine zwitterion
entries.notes: CID 5257127 really is the zwitterion: [NH3+]CC(=O)[O-], IUPAC '2-azaniumylacetate', M  CHG  2   1  -1   3   1 (O1 -1, N3 +1), net charge 0. PubChem title is 'alpha-Glycine'. Carboxylate is stored as one C-O single (O-) and one C=O double (Kekule), but the 3D lengths are nearly equal (1.2618 and 1.2645 A), consistent with the spec's resonanceNote. 3D is an in-vacuo force-field model of a species that is really only stable in water/crystal.

entries.name: L-Alanine (neutral)
entries.notes: Recommend CID 5950 (L-alanine, (2S)-2-aminopropanoic acid; 1 defined stereocentre) rather than CID 602 (DL-alanine, '2-aminopropanoic acid', stereocentre UNDEFINED) or CID 71080 (D-alanine, 2R). L is the proteinogenic enantiomer and the name lookup 'alanine' itself resolves to 5950. Neutral form, no M  CHG. 3 conformers; default returned. 2D record has 1 wedge bond (C4-N3, stereo code 6).

entries.name: L-Alanine zwitterion
entries.notes: CID 7311724 found via name lookup 'L-alanine zwitterion' and verified: SMILES C[C@@H](C(=O)[O-])[NH3+], IUPAC '(2S)-2-azaniumylpropanoate', same InChI stereo layer (/t2-/m0/s1) as L-alanine CID 5950, M  CHG  2   1  -1   3   1 (O1 -1, N3 +1), net 0. PubChem title '(2S)-2-ammoniopropanoate'. Carboxylate C-O 1.2620 / 1.2653 A (near-equal). 2 conformers; default returned.

entries.name: Urea
entries.notes: 3D: both N exactly planar (angle sum 360.0 deg), consistent with the spec's sp2 / trigonal-planar expectation. C=O 1.2293 A, N-H 1.0144 A.

entries.name: Hydronium (H3O+)
entries.notes: CID 123332: PubChem title 'Oxonium', IUPAC 'oxidanium', charge +1, M  CHG  1   1   1 (O1 +1). 3D record EXISTS (200) and is pyramidal: O-H 0.991 A, H-O-H 111.43 deg (angle sum 334.3). No heavy-atom bond.

entries.name: Hydrogencarbonate (HCO3-)
entries.notes: CID 769: title 'Bicarbonate Ion', IUPAC 'hydrogen carbonate', charge -1, M  CHG  1   2  -1 (O2 -1). 3D exists. SURPRISE: the two unprotonated C-O bonds are NOT equal in the PubChem 3D model: C4-O2(-) 1.3958 A (stored single) vs C4=O3 1.3161 A (stored double), and C-OH 1.3536 A - i.e. the O(-) bond is longer than the C-OH bond. The spec's bond card says these two bonds are 'equivalent resonance structures; effective order 1.5', and the measured lengths from this file would visibly contradict that. Planar; O=C-O-H dihedral 0.0.

entries.name: Carbonic acid
entries.notes: CID 767, neutral. 3D exists: C=O 1.2208 A, C-OH 1.3535 A (x2), O-H 0.981 A; planar, both O=C-O-H dihedrals 0 deg (both H syn to the carbonyl O).
